summary.headline: Greenlam Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 18% YoY to INR797 crores, with EBITDA before forex up 48% to INR81 crores and net profit of INR21 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 18% YoY to INR797 crores, with gross margin flat at 52.9% despite input and freight cost spikes from West Asia conflicts. EBITDA before forex rose 48% to INR81 crores, margin 10.2% (up 210 bps), and net profit turned to INR21 crores from a loss of INR15.5 crores a year ago. Chipboard turned EBITDA positive for the first time, while plywood losses narrowed. About INR27 crores of export shipments slipped into Q2 due to container and vessel shortages, and laminate domestic volumes fell about 7.5%.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: Revenue INR596 crores (+7% YoY); sales volume 4.62 million sheets (-6% YoY) due to postponed exports; utilisation 80%; EBITDA margin before forex 13.9% (+70 bps); realisation INR1,240 per sheet (+14% YoY).

segments.name: Plywood and Allied
segments.commentary: Revenue INR106 crores (+20% YoY); EBITDA loss before forex narrowed to INR5 crores from INR9 crores; plywood volume 1.66 million sq m (+19%), realisation INR276 per sq m (+4%), utilisation 39%.

segments.name: Panel and Allied (chipboard)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR95 crores, nearly 4x YoY; EBITDA before forex INR3.4 crores vs loss of INR10 crores; sales volume 41,418 CBM (+167%), realisation INR22,764 per CBM (+15%), utilisation 61% vs 30%.

segments.name: Engineered floors and doors
segments.commentary: Combined revenue about INR29 crores with EBITDA loss of INR1.2 crores, per Q&A.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated FY27 consolidated revenue growth target of 18%, though it did not give volume and value split.
Laminate revenue growth guided at 10-12% for FY27, despite Q1 at about 7%; margin guidance withheld due to raw material uncertainty, with the company citing 15-16% laminate margin previously stated.
Plywood expected to reach EBITDA breakeven in FY27 (likely at some quarter, not necessarily full year); PAT breakeven timing uncertain; utilisation expected near 50% for FY27.
Chipboard utilisation expected to average about 70% in FY27; 18-20% EBITDA margin possible at full utilisation and better mix, expected around FY29.

Capex for FY27 budgeted at INR125-135 crores including about INR70 crores for laminate expansion; net debt expected to fall by about INR100 crores in FY27 and by more than INR150 crores in FY28 per repayment schedules.
capex_capacity: Two new laminate press lines under construction, on track for commercial production by Q4 FY27; equipment ordered, all domestic.
No other large capacity addition planned in FY27; the year is focused on sweating existing assets.
Chipboard: current capacity sufficient for now; value-add (pre-laminated) mix to be increased as utilisation approaches 80-90%; no greenfield or brownfield decision yet.
Plywood: products now available in West and East/Central India; North not planned yet; utilisation target around 50% for FY27.
Decorative veneer, floors and doors: practical utilisation ceiling about 60-65%, given manual processes.
demand_pricing: Domestic laminate volumes fell about 7.5% YoY in Q1 as real estate and project customers deferred dispatches amid cost increases; retail and distribution held up.

Export shipments of about INR27 crores slipped out of Q1 due to container and vessel shortages; management said Q2 impact depends on whether the constraint persists, and the Middle East is about 6-7% of business.

Price increases in April and May, then cuts in June and July, passed on about 7-8% net; increases were driven by chemicals (about one-third of raw material cost, up to 35% of laminate and chipboard content), while wood and paper were stable.
Management said demand should improve as market clarity returns; inventory channel stocking not expected to be materially affected by price cuts.
Chipboard: pre-laminated and HMR products gaining traction; management sees room for realisation gains as value-add products are introduced.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR27 crore export deferral and laminate volume decline make the 10-12% laminate growth guidance credible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the postponed exports, about INR25-30 crores, would close much of the gap and it still expects 10-12% laminate revenue growth; Q1 volume was down 7.5% domestically.

qa_highlights.question: What is the chipboard margin path and utilisation required?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation was 61% in Q1 and is expected to average about 70% in FY27; 18-20% EBITDA margin is achievable at full utilisation and better mix, likely by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: When will plywood reach EBITDA breakeven, and what is the ~INR20 per sq m EBITDA target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects EBITDA breakeven in FY27 but only for a quarter, not the full year; INR20 per sq m (about 8-8.5% margin) needs 80-90% utilisation, versus INR270-275 realisation today.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt reduce?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is expected to fall about INR100 crores in FY27 despite capex of INR125-135 crores; FY28 repayments are above INR150 crores per schedule, and from FY28 cash flow goes mainly to debt reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Why were the laminate and chipboard volumes for prior quarters reclassified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would explain the change offline.

risks_watch: Container and vessel availability; if the export delay persists into Q2, export sales could be affected.
Chemical price volatility (phenol, melamine, urea) tied to West Asia conflict; management did not disclose current market rates.
Domestic laminate demand weakness from real estate and project customers (volume -7.5% in Q1).
Plywood EBITDA breakeven is only guided for one quarter in FY27, with PAT breakeven timing unclear.
Unexplained restatement of prior-year laminate and chipboard volume numbers; to be clarified offline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth and the chipboard and panel turnaround, but cautious and often hedged on exports, raw material direction, plywood breakeven timing and margin guidance. Management avoided quantifying several questions (segment ROI, geographic split, product price comparisons), deferring them offline.
key_quotes: Our chipboard business turned EBITDA positive for the first time with an operating profit of INR3.4 crores before forex and losses in Plywood and Allied segment has continued to narrow.
This is purely a timing matter and the revenue is not lost. It is simply moving into the current quarter.
We still stand by that even though the first quarter growth was close to around 7%, but we still stand by that it can grow 10% to 12%.

adds.what: Two new laminate press lines under construction (domestic equipment ordered), on track for commercial production by Q4 FY27

growth.why: Management reiterated ~18% FY27 consolidated revenue growth and 10-12% laminate growth, backed partly by two laminate press lines due Q4 FY27 (INR70 crore laminate capex), chipboard utilisation rising 30% to 61% and value-add mix, but Q1 laminate volumes fell ~6-7.5% and no volume/value split was given.
